A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RouteFinder and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained content can be matched despite substantial reformatting and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, mixed-backhaul fine-tuning results, and representation analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds multi-depot evaluations, attribute-distribution tests, specialist comparisons, and training analyses.

M1.justification: v3 adapts the existing method for multi-depot routing through per-depot global embeddings, origin-depot decoder features added through EAL, and revised depot masking and multistarts (Appendices A and B). This is a contained procedural extension; the Transformer architecture, MBT, reward normalization, and zero-initialized EAL principles remain.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from 24 variants to 48 through 16 multi-depot variants and eight combining multi-depots with mixed backhauls. Appendix D.1 also adds evaluation under shifted capacities, time windows, and distance limits. The original single-depot coverage and CVRPLIB evaluation are retained.

E2.justification: The existing mixed-backhaul comparison gains zero-shot MTPOMO, MVMoE, RF-POMO, and RF-MoE entries (v2 Table 5.2 versus v3 Table 10). v3 also evaluates separately trained POMO specialists in attribute-shift experiments and five specialist checkpoints in EAL transfer comparisons (Tables 6–8 and 13). The main benchmark comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include capacity and constraint sweeps on 1,000 instances of size 100, three-depot evaluations, and imbalance experiments using 50 epochs of 10,000 instances with time-window sampling probabilities 0.5, 0.25, and 0.10. The main training budget remains unchanged. The retained normalization plot also changes its metric label from average cost to percentage gap without explaining any recomputation.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds separate RMSNorm/SwiGLU ablations, encoder convergence curves, direct MBT loss and convergence comparisons, imbalanced-training studies, attribute-shift sensitivity tests, cross-model t-SNE comparisons, and EAL learning curves. The original reward-normalization analysis and layer-wise t-SNE visualization are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v2 provides no defined uncertainty estimates. v3 introduces shaded bands in plots including Figures 11 and 14, but does not define them or specify associated run counts, seeds, or estimators. It is unclear whether these represent statistical uncertainty or another visualization of variability.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial numerical and qualitative results for attribute shifts, multi-depot transfer, specialist comparisons, and training behavior. Original mixed-backhaul results and CVRPLIB scores are retained. One main-table correction changes RF-MoE's 100-node VRPBLTW objective from 350.808 to 30.808, while retaining the 3.323% gap (Table 5.1 versus Table 1).

T1.justification: Section 3.1 extends the formal problem definition to separate depot and customer sets and multi-depot return requirements; Appendix A extends the corresponding feasibility equations. The existing RL objective and policy-gradient reasoning remain. Appendix C.1 explicates the existing per-variant batch average rather than introducing a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The four central methodological contributions and superiority claim over learned baselines remain. v3 broadens the explicitly claimed coverage from 24 to 48 variants and adds the introduction's claim of covering three times as many variants as previous work. The stronger abstract wording largely repeats claims already present elsewhere in v2.

C2.justification: New interpretations discuss encoder-component convergence tradeoffs, MBT's benefits for minority variants, specialist versus multi-task generalization, and why multi-depot adaptation is harder. Cross-model t-SNE differences are attributed to global attribute embeddings. Existing qualifications about in-distribution specialist performance and remaining gaps to traditional solvers are retained.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands multi-depot generation, masking, decoder-feature, and EAL construction details, and explicitly describes per-variant reward averaging. The reported training-time range changes from 9–48 to 9–24 hours. Conversely, v2's footnote disclosing omission of the depot end-time input disappears; the PDFs do not establish that the earlier experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to GOAL, Karakatič and Podgorelec's multi-depot survey, and Arora et al.'s t-SNE analysis. It removes the explicit criticism of UNCO's performance. The central positioning relative to MTPOMO, MVMoE, and adapter-based transfer remains.

P1.justification: v3 extensively condenses and edits the main narrative and reorganizes the appendices. The backhaul-definition comparison moves to Appendix A.2, EAL implementation receives dedicated subsections, and empirical material is organized into Appendix D. The conclusion is substantially shortened, and acknowledgements and funding are consolidated.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. The attribute schematic adds multi-depots, numerous tables and analytical plots are introduced, and retained displays are resized or relocated. The paired ablation figure is split and recolored as Figures 5 and 8; the original mixed-backhaul table moves into the expanded appendix comparison.

improvement.justification: v2's unseen-attribute evaluation centered on mixed backhauls. v3 substantially strengthens validation through multi-depot and combined-attribute transfer, matched specialist comparisons, and direct tests of encoder components and MBT stability. These address central questions about the framework's generality and training behavior while retaining earlier evidence. Undefined plot bands, unexplained cost-to-gap relabeling, and the removed implementation caveat limit reporting clarity, but do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation.
